title: Cart creation and delivery
description: Create a simulated cart in DummyJSON, merge its ID with the original order and deliver it.
expectedOutcome: Succeeds. Delivery includes the original orderId and the returned cartId. The public service may return a different ID from the fixture.
realNotes: Real systems calls DummyJSON, then Postman Echo. To inspect delivery in a browser, replace the output destination URL with your own Webhook.site URL.

content.yaml:
version: 2
name: sample-cart-chain
# sample: sample-cart-chain
description: Create a simulated cart and deliver the combined order
mode: async
sources:
  - name: order
    trigger: http
    endpoint: /samples/sample-cart-chain
    map: '{ order: $ }'
  - name: cart
    trigger: pull
    depends: order
    from:
      http:
        url: https://dummyjson.com/carts/add
        method: POST
        body: '{ userId: $idm.order.userId, products: $idm.order.items | select item => { id: item.productId, quantity: item.quantity } }'
    map: '{ cart: $ }'
outputs:
  - name: delivery
    map: '{ orderId: $idm.order.id, cartId: $idm.cart.id, cartTotal: $idm.cart.total }'
    destinations:
      http:
        # Optional: replace this URL with your receiving URL from Webhook.site.
        - url: https://postman-echo.com/post
          method: POST

title: Deldo stock import
description: Blob CSV → normalized offers → SQL procedure and versioned Blob snapshot.
expectedOutcome: Completes with the supplied mocks; inspect each connector call and receipt.
realNotes: Configure inbound.connectionString and catalog.connectionString secret grants, create containers and catalog.usp_ImportOffers, and upload the matching sample blob. The synthetic Event Grid input needs the actual blob ETag for real tests.

content.yaml:
# sample: sample-deldo-stock
version: 2
name: sample-deldo-stock
description: >
  A Deldo stock/price file landed in inbound/deldo. Read exactly the blob version the
  event describes, normalise the rows to the shared offer contract, load them into the
  catalog database and keep one snapshot per file version for analysis.
mode: async
ttlSeconds: 2592000   # 30 days of execution history / recovery window

sources:
  # Event Grid BlobCreated notification, ONE event per execution (the ingress adapter
  # splits batches, docs/elwood-requests.md §4). event.elwood re-validates type, path and ETag.
  - name: event
    trigger: http
    endpoint: /samples/sample-deldo-stock
    eventGrid: { subjectPrefix: /blobServices/default/containers/inbound/blobs/deldo/ }
    contentType: json
    map: event.elwood                 # → { event: { supplier, blobPath, fileName, etag, ... } }

  # The file itself, pinned to the version the event announced: if the supplier has
  # already replaced it, the read must fail visibly rather than load new bytes under
  # the old ETag (docs/elwood-requests.md §1). The CSV is pulled as text and parsed
  # explicitly: Deldo is Belgian, expect ';' and decimal comma.
  - name: file
    trigger: pull
    depends: event
    contentType: text
    from:
      blobStorage:
        connectionString: $secrets.inbound.connectionString
        container: inbound
        path: '{$idm.event.blobPath}'
        maxBytes: 26214400
        ifMatch: '{$idm.event.etag}'  # reject a replaced blob
    retry:                            # reads are side-effect free: retry freely
      mode: automatic
      maxAttempts: 5
      delayMs: 2000
      backoffMultiplier: 2
      maxDelayMs: 60000
      transportErrors: true
    map: normalize.elwood             # → { import: {...}, offers: [...] }

outputs:
  # One call per file version. The procedure is idempotent on (blob_path, etag) and
  # returns { import_id, status, offers_loaded }. A timeout after the command was sent
  # may still have committed: no automatic retry, an operator resumes after checking
  # catalog.imports (resume reuses this result if it had succeeded).
  - name: offers-to-sql
    map: '{ import: $.import, offers: $.offers }'
    contentType: json
    retry:
      mode: manual
      allowUncertainWrites: false
    destinations:
      sql:
        - connectionString: $secrets.catalog.connectionString
          storedProcedure: catalog.usp_ImportOffers
          parameter: payload

  # One snapshot per file version; the ETag makes the name unique when the same file name
  # is replaced several times a day, and a redelivery rewrites identical content (no-op).
  # Pipeline Parquet delivery remains unsupported; use JSON for this snapshot.
  - name: snapshot
    map: '{ import: $.import, offers: $.offers }'
    contentType: json
    retry:
      mode: automatic
      maxAttempts: 5
      delayMs: 2000
      allowUncertainWrites: true      # same bytes to the same name: duplicates are harmless
    destinations:
      blobStorage:
        - connectionString: $secrets.inbound.connectionString
          container: analytics
          overwrite: true
          filename: deldo/truck/{$idm.import.receivedDate}/{$idm.import.fileName}.{$idm.import.etag}.json

title: Order echo
description: Transform a synthetic order, POST it to Postman Echo and return the echoed JSON.
expectedOutcome: Succeeds. Response contains orderId DEMO-42 and customer Ada Example.
realNotes: Real systems sends synthetic order data to Postman Echo. No credentials are required.

content.yaml:
version: 2
name: sample-echo-order
# sample: sample-echo-order
description: Transform an order and inspect the HTTP echo
mode: sync
sources:
  - name: order
    trigger: http
    endpoint: /samples/sample-echo-order
    map: '{ order: $ }'
  - name: echo
    trigger: pull
    depends: order
    from:
      http:
        url: https://postman-echo.com/post
        method: POST
        body: '{ orderId: $idm.order.id, customer: $idm.order.customer.name, total: $idm.order.total }'
    map: '{ echoed: $.json, httpStatus: $source.http.statusCode }'
outputs:
  - name: response
    response: true
    map: '{ received: $idm.echoed, httpStatus: $idm.httpStatus }'

title: HTTP 503 failure
description: Observe a failed HTTP source and an output that remains pending.
expectedOutcome: Fails intentionally at source remote with HTTP 503. The response output stays pending.
realNotes: Real systems calls httpbin /status/503. This checks failure reporting; retries belong to M4.

content.yaml:
version: 2
name: sample-http-error
# sample: sample-http-error
description: An intentional HTTP 503 source failure
mode: sync
sources:
  - name: input
    trigger: http
    endpoint: /samples/sample-http-error
  - name: remote
    trigger: pull
    depends: input
    from:
      http:
        url: https://httpbin.org/status/503
        method: GET
outputs:
  - name: response
    response: true
    map: '{ message: "This output must not run after the source fails" }'

title: HTTP timeout
description: Observe a one-second request deadline against a delayed HTTP response.
expectedOutcome: Fails intentionally at source remote. Mock mode simulates the transport failure immediately; real mode exercises the deadline.
realNotes: Real systems calls httpbin /delay/5 with connectionTimeout 1000 ms. Public availability and network errors can affect the observed diagnostic.

content.yaml:
version: 2
name: sample-http-timeout
# sample: sample-http-timeout
description: An intentional HTTP timeout
mode: sync
sources:
  - name: input
    trigger: http
    endpoint: /samples/sample-http-timeout
  - name: remote
    trigger: pull
    depends: input
    from:
      http:
        url: https://httpbin.org/delay/5
        method: GET
        connectionTimeout: 1000
outputs:
  - name: response
    response: true
    map: '{ message: "This output must not run after a timeout" }'

title: Authenticated order chain
description: OAuth2 CRM call followed by a Basic-authenticated HTTP delivery using its result.
expectedOutcome: Completes with the supplied mocks; inspect each connector call and receipt.
realNotes: Real mode writes to your configured endpoints. Configure and grant crm.* and emarsys.* credentials; use controlled test services.

content.yaml:
# sample: sample-order-auth
version: 2
name: sample-order-auth
mode: sync
sources:
  - name: order
    trigger: http
    endpoint: /samples/sample-order-auth
    map: '{ order: $ }'
  - name: crm
    trigger: pull
    depends: order
    from:
      http:
        url: $secrets.crm.url
        method: POST
        body: '{ orderId: $idm.order.id }'
        oauth2:
          tokenUrl: $secrets.crm.tokenUrl
          clientId: $secrets.crm.clientId
          clientSecret: $secrets.crm.clientSecret
    map: '{ crm: $ }'
outputs:
  - name: emarsys
    response: true
    map: '{ orderId: $.order.id, crmId: $.crm.id }'
    destinations:
      http:
        - url: $secrets.emarsys.url
          user: $secrets.emarsys.user
          password: $secrets.emarsys.password

title: Product message → SQL → SAP
description: Enrich a RabbitMQ product event using a SQL procedure, then deliver over HTTP with Basic authentication.
expectedOutcome: Completes with the supplied mocks; inspect each connector call and receipt.
realNotes: Local tests use the supplied trigger input. Real mode calls dbo.GetProduct and SAP; only deployment starts the RabbitMQ subscription. Grant products.sql, products.rabbitmq and sap.* as appropriate.

content.yaml:
# sample: sample-product-sql
version: 2
name: sample-product-sql
mode: async
sources:
  - name: event
    trigger: queue
    rabbitmq:
      connectionString: $secrets.products.rabbitmq
      queue: product-changes
      requireMessageId: true
    map: '{ event: $ }'
  - name: product
    trigger: pull
    depends: event
    from:
      sql:
        connectionString: $secrets.products.sql
        storedProcedure: dbo.GetProduct
        readOnly: true
        parameters:
          id: { type: int, value: '$idm.event.productId' }
    map: '{ product: $[0], event: $idm.event }'
outputs:
  - name: sap
    map: '{ productId: $.event.productId, sku: $.product.sku, quantity: $.product.quantity }'
    retry: { mode: manual }
    destinations:
      http:
        - url: $secrets.sap.url
          user: $secrets.sap.user
          password: $secrets.sap.password
          connectionTimeout: 30000
